body: @benjaminp that seems like an unintended consequence of the change. @ulfjack as the author.

That should be fixed as of 7d6ce010f21c172c7fee9756bd642e90c67f5c92. It still says 'Remote' even though this isn't only remote execution, and it's also showing queue and setup time, which are always zero for local execution (although setup time might be set in the future for local sandboxed execution). I am working on updating the output, except it's been that way internally ~forever, and I am almost certain that there are tools at Google parsing the output, so it might take some time to update all the tools to accept the new output format.
(The critical path computation is also buggy, so don't trust it too much.)
@benjaminp can you confirm that it's fixed at HEAD?

Bazel still always produces `Remote: ` followed by a bunch of 0s. The difference now is that it looks to be possible to change those numbers if Bazel spawn strategies actually produce spawn metrics.

If the current state is an intermediate stage on the way to new output, I'm happy to sit on my hands until that is complete. At least the earlier commits to `CriticalPathComputer` and friends seemed like they were supposed to be pure refactoring, which is why I filed this issue.

body: @agoulti Could you have a look at this?
I have a design doc with a rough plan for what I'd like this to look like, but haven't been able to make much progress due to travel and Bazelcon.

Hi Ulf,

I didn't completely understand the plan.
- Do you plan to remove the "Remote" part but are potentially blocked on the internal tools?
- Do you plan to populate the "Remote" part? Partially populate? (as far as I know, we currently don't have access to queuing and scheduling data when doing remote builds from Bazel)
I'm planning to rewrite the entire end-of-build summary. :-p I'll share the design doc as soon as I can.
We may independently need to update the remote spawn runner (and others) to actually provide timing information so that we can correctly aggregate it.

That sounds like a plan that would take some time to implement.

Do you think it would be desirable to put in a short term stopgap? For example, in Bazel only (not Blaze) remove the "Remote" part until we get it working? Or flag protect it?
@agoulti +1. Rewrites typically take a lot of time and this seems like a simple fix. Wanna submit a patch maybe? :-)
